key_insight: PROBE trains an LLM auditor to act like a realistic user in multi-turn tool-use conversations, revealing policy violations that standard capability or safety benchmarks miss.
engineering_relevance: This gives teams a scalable way to audit deployed agentic systems for compliance issues like pricing, privacy, confirmation, and safety before they surface in production.
method: Formulates agent auditing as a two-player Markov game between auditor and target agent.
Trains auditors with a composite reward for finding violations, maintaining plausible behavior, making conversational progress, and covering diverse policies.
Compares GRPO, DPO, and GFlowNet-based optimization to study which training objective best improves auditing performance.
evidence_signal: Across extensive experiments, PROBE-trained auditors found substantially broader and higher-yield policy violations than same-architecture zero-shot adversaries, even when the auditor was much smaller than the target agent.
watch_item: Performance may depend on how well the reward model and simulated user behavior match real deployment settings, so transfer to new agents and policies needs careful validation.
paper_title: PROBE: Learning to Audit Policy Compliance in Tool-Using LLM Agents
